story_title: As Technical Support Staff, I want to check whether sufficient suitable equipment is available for an event so that I can determine whether its technical requirements can be supported.

acceptance_criteria.text: The system considers the required equipment type.
The system considers the required quantity.
The system considers the event date and time.
Equipment already reserved for overlapping events is excluded from available quantities.
Equipment is treated as unavailable from its collection day (D-1) through the day after its return (Return Day+1), not only during the event's own date and time.
Required transfer and preparation time between the equipment's current location and the event venue is factored into availability.
Equipment recorded as unavailable is excluded.
The system indicates whether sufficient equipment is available.

test_cases.title: Availability check matches on the requested equipment type
test_cases.preconditions:
Catalogue contains 'HD Projector' (12 total, 0 in maintenance, none reserved elsewhere) and 'Wireless Mic' (1 total, all reserved elsewhere for the same dates).
Event 'Town Hall Q4' requests 2x HD Projector only.
Logged in as Technical Support Staff.
The event's equipment request is listed under Equipment Requests with status 'Under review'.
steps: Click Equipment Requests in the side menu
Open the equipment request for the Town Hall Q4 event
Read the HD Projector line under Requested items
test_cases.test_data: Equipment: HD Projector, Requested: 2
test_cases.expected_result:
The HD Projector line shows the chip 'Available' and '12 total − 0 in maintenance − 0 reserved elsewhere = 12 available for these dates'.
Wireless Mic having no free stock has no effect on this line.
No 'Not everything requested is available.' banner is shown.

test_cases.test_data: Wireless Mic: requested 4, available 2. Projector - 4K laser: requested 2, available 3. Video conferencing kit: requested 1, available 0
test_cases.expected_result:
Wireless Mic shows the chip 'Partial', '12 total − 3 in maintenance − 7 reserved elsewhere = 2 available for these dates' and '4 requested, 2 available.'
Projector - 4K laser shows the chip 'Available' and '6 total − 0 in maintenance − 3 reserved elsewhere = 3 available for these dates'.
Video conferencing kit shows the chip 'Unavailable' and '4 total − 1 in maintenance − 3 reserved elsewhere = 0 available for these dates'.
The banner 'Not everything requested is available.' is shown above the requested items.

open_questions: The availability feature is not built yet (src/lib/equipment.ts says checking availability against stock, SPM-48, is a separate ticket). Steps and expected results follow the S-25 Equipment request mockup (design/mockups/EquipmentRequests.dc.html) and UI_DESIGN.md section 7.4: availability appears automatically on the request page, with chips 'Available' / 'Partial' / 'Unavailable', the breakdown 'total - in maintenance - reserved elsewhere = N available for these dates', and the banner 'Not everything requested is available.'. Labels for the equipment time window, the 'venue not yet chosen' note and the per-session layout are proposed and need re-verifying once the screen exists.

Design decisions assumed by these cases (team proposals; customer Q&A #2, #13, #113 leave them to the team): (a) the fixed 2-hour transfer/prep time applies BEFORE the event only, and only when the equipment is not already at the event venue; nothing is added after the event, so EQUIPMENT_LOAD_WINDOW_MS in equipmentWindowFor() must stop adding 2 hours after the event; (b) Return Day is the event's own end date (automatically populated; Q&A #113 allows this); (c) equipment location is a nullable locationVenueId on Equipment where null means ConnectSphere storage (needs a schema change and migration); (d) an event with no venue yet skips transfer time and shows 'Venue not yet chosen'.

AC5 wording: the Jira text says equipment is unavailable 'through Return Day+1', but the customer (Q&A #5, #2) says it is 'available again from Return Day+1'. These cases follow the customer. The Jira acceptance criterion should be corrected. 'Held by <event> until <date>' is assumed to show the day the equipment is available again (Return Day+1).

Only requests with status 'reserved' or 'partially_fulfilled' count against availability (SCHEMA_REFERENCE.md), using quantityReserved. Requests of cancelled, postponed, rejected and draft events are ignored by a TEMPORARY filter on Event.status (TC14) until SPM-37 (Cancel) and SPM-38 (Postpone) release reservations themselves. Revisit when those stories ship.

Zero total stock (TC02) is shown as 'Unavailable' with 0 available. The team wants different wording from an input error, but the wording is not decided. Requesting zero units (TC07) uses the existing message 'Enter a whole number, at least 1.'.

Retired/inactive equipment (TC27): shown as 'Unavailable' on an existing request and hidden from the Add equipment list, following SPM-39. GET /api/equipment does not filter inactive items today, so the hiding is new behaviour.

AC7: 'recorded as unavailable' is defined by SPM-55 (Record Equipment Unavailability: unavailable, damaged or under maintenance, with a reason), which is not built. Only quantityInMaintenance and the inactive flag exist today (TC26, TC27). Add cases once SPM-55 lands.
Sessions of the same event (TC22): it is not defined whether two sessions of one event, on nearby days, block each other's equipment. No case written.
The 'Reserve what is available' button in the mockup belongs to SPM-49 (Reserve Equipment) and is out of scope for SPM-48. Partial reservation is allowed by the customer (Q&A #90).
Rescheduling (TC09) depends on the change flow (SPM-32 / SPM-35), which is not built. The case assumes the event date has already changed.
